minutes.headline: Committee reviewed the revised TCP floor plan and set a Nov 2 meeting for sign-off; Boys and Girls Club space deferred.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the engineer on parking and stormwater, then the superintendent on why the school department needs six rooms for extended day, early learning and community links. Members worked through the revised plan for meeting rooms, storage, toilets and room to grow, and debated whether the Boys and Girls Club can fit. Only prior minutes and adjournment were voted. The architect will send a revised plan to town departments for sign-off, and next meetings were set.

public_comment.topic: Dr Burnham thanked the architect for improved diagrams, especially office space, and noted remaining difficulty with space for extended day.

budget_items.what_was_said: Storage need discussed in floor area and linear feet; a count of boxes was suggested.
After sign-off the design team will move to design documents and a cost estimator will price total construction.
A member explained the state excludes ancillary spaces from its share, so effective reimbursement is lower than the headline rate.
The superintendent said less space would mean reducing the enrollment cap.

A town meeting prep meeting set for Monday November 9.
Boys and Girls Club space to be put on a future agenda; architects continue on the prior direction.
Consensus to leave meeting room three as shown.
Chair and Dave Blatt will review the revised plan before it goes to departments, reporting back by Wednesday morning.
Architect to submit a new plan by mid next week as the schematic design, sent to departments with a sign-off sheet.

what_happened.line: The committee set a Monday, November 2 meeting at 5:30 pm to review department sign-offs on the revised floor plan; no budget votes were taken.
The architect is to submit a new plan by mid next week as the schematic design, to go to town departments with a sign-off sheet.
Boys and Girls Club space was put on a future agenda, and the architects continue on the prior direction.
The committee agreed by consensus to leave meeting room three as shown.
After sign-off, the design team moves to design documents and a cost estimator prices total construction; a town meeting prep meeting was set for November 9.

why_it_matters: The sign-off step and the later cost estimate are what will set the price of the building that voters are asked to fund at Town Meeting, so the space choices made now feed into a future tax commitment.
Space for extended day and the Boys and Girls Club is not settled; the superintendent said less space would mean a lower extended day enrollment cap, which touches families who use that program.
State school-building reimbursement leaves out ancillary spaces, so the share the state pays is lower than the headline rate, and more of the cost falls on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The revised plan and sign-off sheet going to town departments, with the chair and a member reviewing it first and reporting back by Wednesday morning.
The committee meeting on Monday, November 2, and the Town Meeting prep meeting on Monday, November 9.
